lines.text: Ballot Measure Rebuttal Argument Submission Form
If both an argument in favor of and an argument against a measure have been selected for publication in the Sample
Ballot & Official Voter Information Pamphlet, a typed rebuttal to the argument in favor of or the argument against the
measure may be submitted as outlined in this form.
The author(s) of the primary argument of the measure may prepare and submit a rebuttal argument or may authorize
in writing any other person or persons to prepare, submit or sign the rebuttal argument.
A rebuttal argument will not be accepted unless accompanied by this completed form, which shall contain the printed
name(s) and signature(s) of the person(s) submitting it or, if submitted on behalf of a bona fide association of citizens,
the name of the association and the printed name and signature of at least one of its principal officers. Please make
sure you are using proper format before submitting to the Elections Office.
Word count limit for Rebuttal Arguments = 250 words

We must act immediately to raise additional revenues.
Yes on "N" Protects Portola Valley's Financial Stability and Independence. We PO
must act now to ensure our Town's long-term financial viability and avoid losing our 14
status as a locally controlled/incorporated Town. If we don't, we'll be forced to severely 15
cut service levels and become unable to fund critical local needs such as emergency
preparedness, wildfire prevention and maintaining our infrastructure. 7
Yes on "N" Offers an Effective, Near-Term Solution. After extensive analysis
(including significant input by the Finance Committee), a local Real Property Transfer
Tax (RPTT) was selected as the best solution. To enact it, the Town must become a
Charter Town. This will be straightforward, mirroring closely our current administrative
Yes on "N" Adopts a Known Path for Raising Revenues. Many cities in the Bay 16
Area have enacted similar RPTT measures to address severe budget challenges.
RPTTs apply only when a property is sold . The major alternative considered, a parcel
tax, is harder to enact and regressive: imposed on each parcel, each year, forcing
homeowners to suffer an increased annual tax burden no matter what their
Under Measure N, local revenues will be locally controlled. Homeowners will have the
benefit of currently applicable county RPTT exemptions. In implementing Measure N,
the Town may create additional exemptions, and may consider additional measures to
enhance accountability to residents for use of these revenueså
Doing nothing is not an option.
Vote YES on N - protect the future of our Town. end
